result.title: SCALE: Small-Model-First Concept Abstraction with LLM-Guided Experience Internalization
result.summary: Autonomous agents must continually acquire reusable knowledge from experience without relying on costly large language model (LLM) reasoning for every decision. However, existing experience-based approaches often struggle to transform accumulated observations and reasoning into compact knowledge that lightweight models can independently apply. This paper proposes SCALE, a small-model-first framework that integrates selective LLM reasoning, experience-driven concept abstraction, and knowledge internalization. A lightweight model handles routine predictions, while prediction errors and accumulated cross-episode evidence selectively trigger LLM reflection. The LLM analyzes relevant historical experiences, generates positive and negative counterfactual examples, and proposes reusable concept hypotheses. Independently validated concepts are progressively incorporated into hierarchical neural representations, enabling lightweight models to exploit increasingly abstract knowledge. Meanwhile, mastered experiences are excluded from active memory while their original records remain available in a complete archive. Experiments across ten random seeds show that historical recall improves held-out accuracy from 87.11% to 98.28%, hierarchical concept knowledge increases difficult-case accuracy from 55.33% to 66.47%, and abstract archiving reduces active experience records from 6,000 to 1,528.

AI.brief_summary: SCALE 提出以轻量模型为主体的框架：由预测错误与跨回合累积证据选择性触发 LLM 反思，LLM 生成正负反事实样例与可复用概念假设，经独立验证后逐步写入分层神经表示，并把已掌握经验移出活跃记忆而保留归档。
AI.relevance_reason: 按错误信号决定何时调用昂贵 LLM、以及将概念假设内化进分层表示，可能为 LVR 中的「何时进入推理」与把推理结果压缩为 latent 状态提供核查线索，但其无视觉或多模态设定，内化是否构成状态生成需读原文确认。
